premise: The morning of the town's flower festival, Hana's delivery van breaks down, Rin has a deadline at noon, and Takeshi insists on fixing everything to a timetable.

chr_seedHana.text: Sold Kai's bouquet to a nervous proposer

chr_seedTakeshi.text: Took Rin fishing on a rainy Sunday; first fish named "Patch Notes"

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
The van just — died! Right outside the shop, with three hundred tulips still in the back, and Dad already has a clipboard out. Probably.


Kai, come be on my team before he drafts you! And I saved you the last onigiri — salted my hands, not the rice [4].

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
three hundred tulips and a dead van, that's just a normal tuesday. dad's clipboard has timestamps on it, i give it ten minutes before he schedules my breakdown.

he can have me after noon, i'm not missing this deadline. fight me, dad.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Right on schedule. Van dies, family panics, Dad fixes it. Clipboard's got two columns — tulips loaded by 9:15, Rin's deadline by noon. Nobody argues with the timetable.
Kai, you're on flowers. And hey — a broken van is like a late train: nobody's happy, but everybody gets where they're going eventually.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
\I put on both my gloves and then realized I'd already taken the van keys out. So that's going great!!


Okay, Kai and I load the tulips, Dad drives the second car — and Rin, eat something before noon, you always go feral on deadlines.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
the timetable has a *second car* scheduled. dad's been waiting his whole life for a van to die so he could deploy the second column.

i'll eat, but if i get one crumb on this keyboard i

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
You eat at the table, Rin. Not at the keyboard. That's a rule, not a suggestion. Second car's already warmed up — and your sister's right about the feral thing.
Tulips first, code second. Every train stops at every station, even the express. Alright — what do you call three hundred tulips in a hurry? A flower-powered engine. Let's move.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Three hundred tulips and Dad's making train jokes — I love this family, mostly.

The keyboard survives, Rin. Eat at the table, then go be brilliant, and Kai and I will have the stall half-built before you're done! <!-- maybe cut -->

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
fine, table. but i'm eating in four minutes flat, that's technically a meal experience.

good luck with the stall. i'll be done by noon and then i'm judging the flower arrangements. objectively.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Four minutes isn't a meal, it's a train doing a rolling stop. Sit, chew, breathe. Then go be brilliant.
And Hana — half-built? No. Fully built by 10:40. I've got it on the clipboard. Right on schedule, ladies. All aboard.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Objectively judging my own flowers, bold of my little sister — she'll give the tulips a five and the daisies a ten, probably.

Alright, Kai, apron on! Half-built by 10:40 means Dad wins, and I refuse to let the clipboard

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
the clipboard always wins, hana. that's its whole power. you can't out-schedule the column.

apron on, kai. i'll be at the table, being a model citizen for exactly four minutes.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Clipboard undefeated since 1989. Some things you don't argue with — timetables, weather, and your little sister's judging panel.
Apron on, Kai. Buckets by the van, two per trip. Tulips don't wait for anybody. Hana — we move in sixty seconds. Right on schedule.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Sixty seconds! That's barely enough time to trip over one bucket, Dad, and I need at least three attempts — probably.

Kai, grab the yellow tulips, you remember they're my favorite, right? Okay, go go go, the clipboard is watching!!

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
yellow tulips, memorized. she only mentions them every festival since we were kids. not that i keep track. go, the clipboard's started its countdown.

i'm eating. four minutes. don't time it, dad.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Wouldn't dream of timing you, Rin. I'm just noting the clock in my head. And on the clipboard. Yellow tulips, front left, that's your sister's corner.
Sixty seconds starting now — actually, fifty-three. Right on schedule

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Fifty-three!! Dad, that's not fair, I hadn't put my gloves on yet!

Kai — yellow tulips first, they're the heart of the whole stall. Rin, eat. If you finish in three minutes I'll be suspicious

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
three minutes, forty seconds. suspicious yet, hana? no. good. now i'm at the keyboard and the rest of you are background noise until noon.

go build the stall. i

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Gloves are a luxury, Hana. Buckets aren't. Grab and go — I'll catch anything you drop, that's what dads are for. Rin's at the keyboard, clock's ticking.
Forty seconds. Move like a train leaving the station — no dawdling, no looking back. Right on schedule.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Kai, I dropped a bucket. Dad caught it. We're a very well-oiled machine and I've only almost cried once!!

Yellow tulips in the front corner, daisies on the right — oh, this is going to be so pretty you'll have

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
one cry before 10am is a new personal best, hana. proud of you. genuinely. no undercut.

i'll come look when it's done. back at noon.

lines.speaker: director
lines.text: The festival committee calls: they need twice as many sunflowers by two o'clock.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
One cry is on schedule, two means we're doing it right. Caught the bucket, kept the tulips dry, nobody's toes got it.
Stall's coming together faster than a bullet train. Hana — center ribbon. Kai — hold this end. Right on schedule.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Twice as many?? Two o'clock is barely four hours and the stall isn't even up — okay, okay, breathe, Hana.

Dad, please tell me the clipboard has a sunflower column in it. Kai, baby, we're going to need a bigger second car.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
did the committee just double the order? on festival morning? that's not a schedule, that's a crisis with a timetable.

so. sunflower run at two, my deadline at noon.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Clipboard's got a margin at the bottom for exactly this. Sunflower column — added, 11:10. Crisis with a timetable just became a timetable.
Rin codes till noon, then she's my navigator. Hana and Kai finish the stall. I find sunflowers. Right

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Dad, you just added a whole column for me — okay, I'm not going to cry twice before ten, I'm not, I'm NOT.

Rin, code. Kai, ribbon. Dad, you're my favorite person alive right now, don't tell Rin — it's temporary, probably.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
temporary's generous. i'll take navigator duty, i know every back road in this town better than the map does.

code now. commentary later.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Temporary favorite — I'll take it. Don't tell your mother, but there's a third column, and it's her birthday next week.
Ribbon, Kai. Sunflowers at 11:10. Rin, seatbelt by noon

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Case in point: everyone's so busy no one will even notice it's crooked! Dad wins, tulips win, and I got both my favorite people on ribbon duty.

Third column for Mom's birthday — see, this is why the clipboard always wins.
